title: WorkflowStep
description: An ordered, user-facing action within exactly one UserWorkflow, stating what the user does or experiences at that point in the journey and its observable result, described without reference to screens, routes, components or code. Each step names one position in one workflow; the same action in a different workflow is a different step. Use UserWorkflow instead when the element is the whole goal-directed journey made up of several steps, rather than one position within it. Use Feature instead when the element is a reusable unit of user-visible functionality that may be exercised by steps in many workflows, rather than a point in a particular journey. Use Capability instead when the element describes an ability the product has regardless of any user sequence, with no ordering or user action attached.

sequence.description: Position of the step within its UserWorkflow (1-based)

action.description: What the user does or experiences at this step, from the user's point of view (e.g. 'Requests a password reset link')

outcome.description: Observable result of the step for the user (e.g. 'Receives an email containing a reset link')

optional.description: Whether the workflow can complete without this step

x-dr-standard: No direct ArchiMate 3.2 Strategy element; closest is a sub-process in ArchiMate 3.2 §8.3.1 Business Process decomposition, combined with the user-journey or story-map step of product-management practice
x-dr-evidence: Numbered 'When'/'Then' lines inside a Gherkin Scenario or acceptance-criteria list that describe a user action and its visible result
test.step('...') or cy.step-style blocks inside an end-to-end test (Playwright, Cypress) named after a user action within a journey test
A user-journey, onboarding or story-map document (or wizard step config array) listing ordered steps with titles like 'Enter email' and 'Confirm code'
